subject: DPA: clarifying erase lifecycle, backup TTLs, and residency carveouts
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@aurorahealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Delgado <m.delgado@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2029-05-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on erase lifecycle / backups in proposed DPA

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the redline. We digested most sections but have a few specific asks that will determine whether we can accept the standard DPA language or need a localized addendum. High-level items:

- Backup TTLs: Aurora's security team requires that backups containing customer data be purged within 30 days of primary-data deletion unless they are retained for a stated legal hold. Your proposal references a 90-day backup window. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a shorter backup deletion SLA for Aurora's account or provide a technical compensating control (e.g., encryption key destruction tied to retention)?

- Certified proof of erasure: We need an auditable receipt that shows deletion occurrence and scope (primary vs. snapshot vs. cold archive). A simple acknowledgement email won't suffice. Are you able to provide a standardized certificate or automated manifest we can reference in audits?

- Jurisdictional carveouts: We operate in multiple states and some data must remain onshore. We need clear language on how Redwood will map on-prem / VPC customer pins to geofenced storage and what fallback happens when onshore capacity is exhausted.

I'll attach the PDF of our internal data handling requirements and the tracked redline from legal. Can we set up a short sync today to go through the three bullets? Marcus will join for the backup/ops questions.

Best,
Elaine
Director, Vendor Security
Aurora Health

Attachment: Aurora_DPA_track_changes_v2.docx (docx, 124KB)
Attachment: aurora-data-requirements.pdf (pdf, 678KB)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-08T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on erase lifecycle / backups in proposed DPA

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then proposing a short call at 1:30pm PT to align: 

- Backup TTLs: We don't currently offer a blanket 30-day backup purge for all customers because of cross-region replication and the way snapshots are retained for recovery objectives. That said, for enterprise customers we can offer an account-level operational commitment: a 30-day purge on customer-writable snapshots and warm backups when configured behind a Dedicated or Private deployment. For hosted customers we can provide key-rotation-based access revocation plus a documented runbook for deletion and compensating controls.

- Certified proof of erasure: Redwood can produce an automated erasure manifest (JSON output) that includes object ids, timestamps, and job ids. We can include a notarized audit statement as an addendum for customers that require it. I attached our runbook PDF for the erase lifecycle.

- Jurisdictional carveouts: We support geofencing and can pin primary data to specific cloud regions. When onshore capacity is full we have a predefined fallback policy: 1) attempt provisioning additional onshore pool; 2) if not feasible, failover to a nearshore region with strict audited access; 3) notify the customer and wait for explicit direction. We can push the fallback step to ‘manual escalation’ for Aurora if that is a hard requirement.

Call? 1:30pm PT today works for Karhik and me.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-erase-lifecycle-runbook.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Marcus Delgado <m.delgado@aurorahealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2029-05-08T13:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on erase lifecycle / backups in proposed DPA

Thanks — quick clarifying notes from ops: 

- If "account-level operational commitment" only applies to Dedicated/Private, we need to document the migration trigger and timeline. Many of our systems start on hosted and later graduate to a Dedicated footprint; the DPA needs a defined promise window (e.g., 30 days from receiving migration notice + 14-day provisioning buffer) that seats the 30-day backup purge guarantee.

- On "notarized audit statement": we need the technical detail. Is the manifest generated at deletion time stored in a tamper-evident log (e.g., signed S3 object + KMS key rotation) or will it be an on-demand statement from Redwood's security team? For third-party auditors we prefer the tamper-evident manifest approach.

- Regarding fallback: manual escalation is acceptable; define SLA for notification and time-to-escalate (we propose notification within 1 hour and escalation decision within 24 hours).

I'll join the 1:30pm PT call.

—Marcus
Sr. Manager, Cloud Ops
Aurora Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@aurorahealth.com>, Marcus Delgado <m.delgado@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-09T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on erase lifecycle / backups in proposed DPA — follow up and proposed language

Hi Elaine and Marcus — thanks again for the call earlier. Per our notes, I'm summarizing the proposed redline language and next steps so legal and ops can work in parallel: 

1) Backup deletion SLA (new clause proposal): "For Dedicated and Private customers who provide written migration notice, Redwood will purge customer-writable snapshots and warm backups within thirty (30) days after the later of (a) the customer's deletion request or (b) the completion of provisioning of the Dedicated/Private capacity described in the Customer Order. For Hosted customers, Redwood will perform logical access revocation within seven (7) days and will provide configurable key-rotation-based destruction; physical removal of replicated backups will follow the standard backup retention schedule unless otherwise contractually agreed."

2) Certified erasure manifest (new exhibit): "Redwood will generate a signed erasure manifest at the time of deletion containing object identifiers, deletion timestamps, job ids, and the initiating principal. Manifests will be stored in a tamper-evident store (signed objects with KMS-backed keys) for a minimum of ninety (90) days and made available to the customer and to auditors upon approved request. Redwood may provide a notarized audit statement upon reasonable request for an additional fee as set forth in the Order Form."

3) Geofencing fallback (operational SLA): "If onshore capacity is exhausted, Redwood will (i) attempt to procure additional onshore pool resources within forty-eight (48) hours, (ii) if procurement is not feasible within forty-eight (48) hours, Redwood will failover to the pre-agreed nearshore region and notify the customer within one (1) hour. If the customer elects to require manual escalation, Redwood will notify the customer within one (1) hour and await escalation direction; Redwood will then act on the customer's decision within twenty-four (24) hours."

Action items: 
- Redwood legal to push redline with the three clauses above into the tracked Word doc by EOD May 10. (Kimberly)
- Redwood ops to document the tamper-evident manifest technical spec and provide an implementation ETA. (Karthik — target May 17)
- Aurora to confirm whether the notarized audit statement is required for all erasures or only for regulated datasets. (Elaine — please confirm)

If that summary matches your expectations I'll include the bullet language as a proposed DPA addendum. 

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Contracts
Redwood Inference
